description:
User-defined PR5: plan execution through Jido and email adapters, exact SMTP MIME sizing, failure policies, partial outcomes, confirmation and history. Depends on PR4 contracts/planning. Reuse DeliveryConfirmation and existing Engine event. No AttachDocuments (PR6), workflow/notification integration (PR7), or replacement of PR2 FileSettings/resolver. Detailed executor and PR5 finalization tasks must be added before implementation; existing transport tasks are carried here. Reuse zaq-h2i.4 for real adapter prerequisites. Planning only.

Approved PR5 behavior (user confirmation, 2026-11-27): Preserve the reference root-publication policy. Under abort, stop publication after failure and retain earlier confirmed results. Under continue, an unconfirmed root send remains unconfirmed; promote the next eligible candidate with the original answer, then thread subsequent messages under the confirmed root. Never retry the failed operation itself. Possible duplicate answer text after an uncertain provider acceptance is an accepted consequence of this policy. This supersedes the audit suggestion to stop dependent publications after an unconfirmed root. Implement with current separate Plan and Outgoing.attachments contracts; do not restore Outgoing.Delivery. Regression acceptance: a timed-out first root is invoked once, the next candidate publishes the original answer once, later messages use the confirmed root ID, and the report preserves the original uncertainty and partial outcome. Reference: ../zaq-feat-channel-files/test/zaq/channels/delivery/executor_test.exs, test "continue retains an unknown send and promotes the next candidate with the original answer". This approval settles this policy only; it does not approve unrelated reference architecture or change existing test expectations wholesale. Action reuse: planning update only; no executable operation changes.

Approved concurrency contract (2026-11-27): Preserve reference execution behavior. Abort publishes sequentially and stops after failure. Continue establishes a confirmed root before running ready threaded replies concurrently; independent messages may run concurrently without a root. Default maximum concurrency is four operations per delivery attempt, configurable through the existing runtime configuration boundary. Reports retain stable plan order even when completion and recipient-visible order differ. Executor acceptance tests must cover the configured bound, root-before-replies ordering, sequential abort and stable results. Reference: delivery/executor.ex and delivery/executor_test.exs in ../zaq-feat-channel-files. Carry this requirement into the pending executor issue; keep Plan separate from Outgoing.

Approved preparation-failure contract (2026-11-27): Preserve reference behavior for attachment acquisition/preparation failures before publication. Abort stops without publishing messages after preparation failure. Continue publishes the answer with usable attachments and reports failed attachments; if none can be prepared, publish the answer as text only while retaining attachment failure evidence. Failed attachments must never be reported as delivered. This does not authorize fallback after uncertain publication or settle unresolved transport-configuration handling. Apply policy in the Channel execution layer using current shared settings; keep the planner pure, original attachment indices stable, and Plan separate from Outgoing. Do not restore the old selection-failure notice route. Acceptance tests: mixed valid/invalid preparation under both policies; no usable files under continue; later direct-send group preparation failure prevents every publication under abort; failed acquisition is not retried for reused indices; outcomes retain failures and confirmed-only attachment evidence. Reference: ../zaq-feat-channel-files/test/zaq/channels/email_bridge/outgoing_attachments_test.exs and delivery/group_execution_test.exs. Planning update only; no code or existing tests changed.

Approved operation-deadline contract (2026-11-27): Preserve a configurable default timeout of 30,000 ms per upload, send or edit, including sole sends and existing-message edits. Execute transport operations in supervised tasks and terminate timed-out local tasks. Timeout/task exit remains unconfirmed, since local termination does not prove provider rejection. Never retry the operation automatically; apply approved abort/continue and root-promotion rules to subsequent operations. This is a per-operation deadline, not a whole-attempt deadline. Executor regression tests must cover upload/send/edit timeouts, task exits, earlier-confirmation preservation, unattempted steps under abort and no repeated invocation. Runtime configuration must retain the established injectable config boundary. Planning update only; implementation remains pending.

Approved requirements-resolution failure policy (2026-11-27): Preserve reference behavior. When attachment transport requirements cannot be resolved, continue may deliver the original answer as text only, without acquiring or uploading attachments, while retaining each attachment configuration failure in the outcome. Abort returns the failure without sending. The Channel execution/orchestration layer applies the selected connection shared failure policy; TransportRequirements.resolve/2 and the metadata planner return errors unchanged. Do not restore bridge-owned requirements resolvers or fabricate capability support. Fallback requires a valid text-delivery connection and must obey its transport constraints; it does not bypass authentication, connector selection or message sizing. Optional unresolved byte limits accepted by the current resolver are not resolution errors. Acceptance: continue text fallback with zero acquisition/upload; abort no send; failed attachments never confirmed; selected connection policy and text limits retained; accepted optional unresolved limits do not trigger fallback. Reference: ../zaq-feat-channel-files/test/zaq/channels/delivery/executor_test.exs, requirements-error fallback test. Carry this into pending executor/API integration issues. Planning only; no code/test changes.

Approved exact SMTP sizing contract (2026-11-27): Prepare complete encoded MIME, including attachments and headers; measure against the selected connection message limit; submit the measured representation without rebuilding it. Re-encode and revalidate when final thread/continuation headers change before submission. Disable automatic SMTP retries. Confirmation means relay acceptance, not recipient delivery. A rejected oversized continuation preserves earlier confirmed messages. Verify compatibility with current Swoosh/gen_smtp dependencies before choosing the preparation/submission seam; do not blindly copy reference hardcoded version checks. Acceptance: exact boundary succeeds, over-limit fails before submission, continuation-header overflow retains earlier confirmation, measured MIME matches actual SMTP submission including framing, no automatic retry, selected sender/config/envelope isolation, prepared bytes excluded from logs/telemetry. Reference: ../zaq-feat-channel-files/lib/zaq/channels/email_bridge/smtp_sender.ex and test/zaq/channels/email_bridge/outgoing_attachments_test.exs. Planning update only; implementation pending.

PR5 scope audit against reference feat/channel-files at 8d987fa5c and current PR5/PR4 boundary f2681e07b (2026-11-27). Read-only source/test inspection; tests were not executed. Findings are proposed planning additions, not approval to import the reference implementation.

The current epic has only zaq-6rc.5/.6/.7. Those cover transport and confirmation but do not fully specify the shared runtime or production entry-point integration.

Proposed missing work packages:
1. Execution/outcome contracts: define a Channel-local executor input using separate Outgoing, Plan and trusted connection/runtime context; define per-step confirmed/failed/unattempted facts, uploaded-only versus delivered attachment indices, partial results and not-sent versus unconfirmed failures. Preserve stable original indices. Keep raw provider errors private. Reuse Plan/Step and DeliveryConfirmation; do not copy Outgoing.Delivery or selection-stage errors.
2. Shared execution lifecycle: validate dependency graph and references before effects; acquire each original Record at most once per attempt, including cached acquisition failures; reuse Preparation.acquire/3 and Attachments.validate_group/2 / validate_upload_group/2; validate encoded requests; release acquired bytes/prepared payloads when no remaining step needs them. Specify abort/continue behavior separately for preparation, upload and publication. Upload success alone cannot confirm message delivery. Define timeout/task-exit behavior without automatic retries. Confirm concurrency and root-selection rules before implementation.
3. Channels.Api integration: the current :deliver_outgoing handler still calls bridge.send_reply/2 directly. Wire the shared snapshot/resolver, separate plan construction and executor into that existing path, preserving text-only delivery, formatting, canonical answer versus provider body, trusted actor/opts, selected connector and streamed-message identity. Keep API orchestration thin and transport policy in its owning runtime. Do not add the reference report_file_failure/build_failure_plan notice route.
4. Integrated regressions and finalization: real internal API -> bridge -> external transport -> confirmation paths; group failure matrix/property tests; text parity; privacy and concurrent-attempt isolation. Plan owning service documentation, review, post-review coverage and final validation under docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md. Establish whether any feature E2E belongs here or in PR7; backend integration tests are immediately in scope.

Strengthen existing tasks:
- zaq-6rc.5: actual adapter upload/prepare/send/edit capability prerequisites (reuse zaq-h2i.4), actual provider IDs, multiple upload batches, partial upload references, stream-placeholder edit semantics, callbacks exactly once after confirmation, callback/status/reporting failure must not resend.
- zaq-6rc.6: freeze selected SMTP sender/config/envelope; measure and submit the same encoded MIME bytes; remeasure continuation/thread headers before submission; reject malformed prepared payloads; avoid transport retry/telemetry leaking prepared bytes. Reference SmtpSender bypasses generated Mailer via version-checked encoder/gen_smtp; re-evaluate compatibility and ownership rather than copy hardcoded version gates.
- zaq-6rc.7: per-message canonical body/thread and confirmed-only attachments; preserve partial/unknown evidence and uploaded-only distinction; strip content before Engine dispatch; source materialization handles cannot serve as provider locators; unavailable history must preserve transport outcome without repeat sends.

Reference evidence:
lib/zaq/channels/delivery/executor.ex: execute, prepare_execution, run_upload_groups, run_continue, run_steps, release_attachment_content, report.
lib/zaq/channels/delivery/error.ex; api.ex: deliver_reply/report_file_failure; email_bridge/smtp_sender.ex and smtp_sender/prepared.ex; delivery/confirmation.ex.
Tests: delivery/executor_test.exs, delivery/group_execution_test.exs, delivery/confirmation_test.exs, jido_chat_delivery_test.exs, email_bridge/outgoing_attachments_test.exs, email_file_delivery_integration_test.exs.

Decisions still needed: retain reference continue-mode root promotion after an unconfirmed send (may duplicate answer text if the provider accepted the timed-out request); retain bounded reply concurrency; define text-only fallback after preparation/requirements errors under the revised pure planner; choose exact SMTP encoder/submission seam. These are not implied by the seven-PR split.

Current architecture wins: Outgoing.attachments only; Plan remains separate and metadata-only; shared PR2 resolver/settings authoritative; unresolved limits remain unresolved; keep existing DeliveryConfirmation name/event; no PR6 AttachDocuments/Agent selection or PR7 workflow/notification wiring. No existing tests changed.

Action reuse assessment: audit only, no executable changes. Proposed runtime is Channel-local infrastructure, reusing existing preparation/planning/domain APIs and extending existing bridges/reporter; no new agent Action/tool or parallel send/history route. Detailed issue contracts/dependencies must be completed after the unresolved behavioral choices, before implementation.
